extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing/submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guidance used by PLOS ONE to determine whether a manuscript is suitable for publication; covers acceptable article types, originality, technical quality, ethics, reporting, and data availability. Intended to guide authors on what will be considered and grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study presents the results of primary scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of primary scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE is designed to communicate primary scientific research across the natural sciences, medical research, engineering, and related social sciences and humanities. The journal will not consider reviews, case reports, study protocols, hypothesis/proposal papers, letters/commentaries/essays, opinion pieces, policy papers, clinical practice guidelines, other secondary literature, monographs, or unsolicited collection reviews/overviews. The journal will consider certain article types such as systematic reviews (only if methods ensure comprehensive and unbiased sampling), submissions describing methods/software/databases/tools (if they follow appropriate reporting guidelines), qualitative research (only if adhering to appropriate study design and reporting guidelines), and studies reporting negative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results reported have not been published elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE does not accept studies already published in whole or in part in the peer-reviewed literature; all figures should be original and not previously published. Submissions currently under consideration elsewhere will not be considered. Depositing manuscripts on preprint servers (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv) or publication as a thesis is permitted and does not affect consideration; conference presentations are acceptable. Replication studies or work very similar to existing work must provide a sound scientific rationale and clearly reference and discuss existing literature; submissions that are derivative without adequate justification will likely be rejected. See the journal's preprint server policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical quality and sufficient methodological detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must be conducted rigorously with appropriate controls and replication. Sample sizes should be large enough to produce robust results where applicable. Methods and reagents must be described in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to reproduce the experiments. Statistical analyses should be performed to a high technical standard. Failure to provide necessary methodological detail or rigorous conduct may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data must support the conclusions drawn; submissions will be rejected if interpretations are unjustified or inappropriate. Authors should avoid overstating conclusions. Discussion of possible implications is allowed only if clearly identified as hypotheses rather than definite conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article intelligibility and standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts, so submitted language must be clear, correct, and unambiguous. Manuscripts with poor language that are difficult to understand may be rejected or the journal may recommend authors obtain independent editorial/manuscript editing services prior to revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research meets ethics of experimentation and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research must be conducted to the highest ethical standards; the journal may apply standards more stringent than local requirements. Approval from the relevant body is required for studies involving humans (including observational/survey-based studies and those with personal data), animals (including observational studies), non-commercial cell lines, field sampling, and work with potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why it was not required. PLOS ONE is a member of COPE and expects compliance with best practices in publication ethics regarding authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. For details, see the Editorial Policies and Submission Guidelines; contact the editorial office for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting guidelines and community data-availability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results must be reported rigorously according to community/discipline-specific reporting guidelines (see submission guidelines for details). Authors must follow standards for data deposition in publicly available resources (for example, repositories for gene sequences, microarray expression data, structural studies, etc.). Failure to comply with community standards for reporting or data deposition may lead to rejection. See the journal's data availability policy for further requirements.
